messages:
jen_support: received a report from ACME about large reserved GPU-hours on their Dedicated pool rp-987 for 2026-03-10 00:00-06:00 UTC, but token usage is minimal. Customer pasted invoice snippet: 'reserved_hours: 18.5', 'tokens: 12k' — they think we're charging warmup or idle instances. Can triage? /cc @kevin_sre @carl_backend @maya_billing

kevin_sre: looking. Do we have pool id and workspace? Also need sample request_id or instance ids if available.

jen_support: pool rp-987, workspace acme-corp, invoice id inv-ACME-20260310, sample request_ids: r_abc123 (03:14:22 UTC), r_def456 (04:02:10 UTC). Customer notes 98% of GPU hours came in 3 x 5-6min bursts while token burn was <500 tokens each.

carl_backend: thanks. Initial hypothesis: warmup autoscaler or node churn causing hourly metering to bill partial hours; also possible warmup job or background init using full GPU. I'll pull serving logs and instance lifecycle events. Will check whether min_instances >0 and warmup flag set.

metering-bot: automated metering snapshot attached: pool: rp-987, timeframe: 2026-03-10T00:00:00Z - 2026-03-10T06:00:00Z, total_gpu_hours: 18.21, billed_hours: 19.0, total_tokens: 12,457, token_based_billing: 0.013 tokens/sec avg.

kevin_sre: check host-level uptime — sometimes host restart during billing window re-allocates full hour to customer due to rounded billing. Query: internal_telemetry.query("SELECT sum(active_gpu_seconds)/3600 as hours, count(distinct instance_id) FROM serving.metric WHERE pool='rp-987' AND ts BETWEEN ...")

carl_backend: ran query — results: active_gpu_seconds=65556s (~18.21h) but there are 4 instances with overlapping starts: inst-22, inst-73, inst-77, inst-81. Two of those show init logs 'model load' and 'warmup: true' at start time.

carl_backend: snippet of logs:
```
[03-10T03:09:15Z] inst-73 model load start
[03-10T03:10:02Z] inst-73 warmup complete, kv-cache primed
[03-10T03:10:10Z] inst-73 accepted request r_abc123 (tokens_in: 120)
```

carl_backend: warmup time was ~47s but instance stayed up for ~5m after which it was terminated. Warmup uses 100% GPU and counts to active_gpu_seconds. That explains GPU-hours vs tokens mismatch.

maya_billing: thanks — can we confirm whether billed reserved_hours rounds up to nearest 1 hour per instance? customer seeing 19.0 billed but active 18.21. If rounding rules applied per-instance, overlaps cause extra billing.

kevin_sre: billing pipeline currently aggregates hourly per instance and rounds up to nearest 15min on meter ingestion, but invoice line items round to nearest 0.1 hour in presentation. The 19.0 probably due to per-instance rounding + rounding in invoice generation. I will produce a breakdown: raw_seconds by instance.

metering-bot: breakdown (raw_seconds): inst-22: 14400s, inst-73: 330s, inst-77: 16200s, inst-81: 256s

jen_support: customer also said they saw burst routing from fallback pool. Could some requests be routed to dedicated but served by fallback causing warmup? They noticed a 'fallback: true' header earlier.

carl_backend: good catch — fallback routing can spin up instances in dedicated pool to satisfy SLA. Check routing logs for 'fallback' decisions.

kevin_sre: routing trace for request r_def456 shows: route_decision: fallback_to_dedicated -> inst-81 created at 04:01:12Z -> accepted request at 04:02:10Z. So short-lived warmup instance to serve fallback. Combine these events with per-instance rounding and it's plausible.

carl_backend: repro steps to validate locally:
1) Create test workspace and bind model with reserved pool rp-test-XYZ and set min_instances=0 and fallback_policy=allow_dedicated
2) Send a single short request that triggers fallback (simulate backend overload)
3) Observe instance spin-up logs and query internal_telemetry for active_gpu_seconds
Commands:
```
# curl to trigger
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/requests -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"acme-13b","input":"hi"}'
# query telemetry
internal_telemetry.query("SELECT * FROM serving.metric WHERE instance_id='inst-xxx' ORDER BY ts")
```

carl_backend: mitigation options:
- Short term: apply invoice adj / credit for warmup-primed hours where token burn < X within N minutes (propose threshold)
- Mid term: change billing ingestion to prorate on active_gpu_seconds across pool instead of per-instance rounding
- Ops: add metric and alert for 'warmup-heavy pool' where warmup_seconds/active_seconds > 0.05

maya_billing: for customer fairness, propose provisional credit equal to the overlapping rounding delta: 0.79 hours -> calculate $ amount. I'll prepare credit memo draft pending confirmation.

jen_support: thanks. Customer asks for ETA. Can someone take ownership for communication and provide a write-up?

kevin_sre: I'll own the tech write-up and provide instance-level breakdown by EOD PST. carl_backend will draft repro steps and suggested infra mitigations. maya_billing will prepare credit memo and hold invoice if possible.

jen_support: I'll send interim update to customer: 'We reproduced behaviour; short-lived warmup instances + per-instance rounding caused the discrepancy. We're preparing credits and infra fix plan.'

carl_backend: follow-ups: add instrumentation to show 'warmup_time' per instance in telemetry, and add flag to meterer to exclude warmup-only instances under 2min from reserved-hour billing (requires policy review).

kevin_sre: recorded action items:
- kevin: publish per-instance breakdown (ETA: 2026-03-11 18:00 UTC)
- carl: add repro guide and open infra PR for warmup metric (ETA: 2026-03-18)
- maya: draft credit memo and post to billing queue (ETA: 2026-03-12)
- jen: customer comms (ETA: 2026-03-11 12:00 UTC)

jen_support: noted, thanks all :thumbsup:
